target_customer: Factory owners and production heads at Indian auto component and other manual-assembly manufacturers
problem: Manual assembly lines lack real-time visibility into operator output and SOP adherence. Optifye points AI cameras at workstations and shows productivity on a dashboard.
business_model: Hardware plus software subscription for factories (pricing not found)
product_category: Computer vision workforce and line productivity monitoring

founders.name: Vivaan Baid
education: Duke University, computer science and psychology
founders.background_notes: YC page: family has run a manufacturing company for years.

founders.name: Kushal Mohta
education: Duke University, B.S.E. electrical and computer engineering and B.S. computer science
founders.background_notes: YC page: built a system that raised efficiency 105% on semi-automated lines at a gears maker; family runs several manufacturing plants.

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision for operator actions and SOP steps on varied assembly lines, plus camera deployment in factories, is standard but demanding for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Vision models and cameras are commodity. Advantage is factory relationships and workflow data in India.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Western vendors such as Invisible AI (raised $15M in 2022 per Futurism-era coverage) served factories. No source found showing an incumbent copying the India wedge.

market_need_then: The company says it works with 5 of the 10 largest auto component makers in India. Founders come from manufacturing families, indicating access to buyers.

branding.domain_note: Uses optifye.ai; acquisition history not found.
branding.community_and_virality: In February 2025 a YC demo video that labeled a worker 'Number 17' went viral; TechCrunch reported YC deleted its posts after backlash over worker surveillance, and Gizmodo and others called it dystopian.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand became known mainly through a negative viral moment tied to the demo, not through brand work.

outcome_analysis: Optifye is active with no reported exit or shutdown. Founders with manufacturing family ties claimed customers among India's largest auto component makers. In February 2025 its demo drew intense criticism and YC removed its posts, a reputational hit, but searches found no later layoffs or closure. Funding is unverified beyond YC.
notes: Funding unverified: SeedTable lists $500K dated February 2025, VCBacked lists pre-seed dated March 2025 with amount undisclosed and YC as investor; aggregators only, so no round recorded. Competitor result pages were undated vendor comparison pages, so list left empty. Company website fetch was blocked by a rate-limited safety check, so site content is not used. One outlet says a different name was a co-founder in a query I made; ignored, only YC-page founders are listed.
